children.translated_text: Salutations to <s>Śrī Gaṇeśa</s>.
Now begins the <s>Bandīmocana</s> (Liberation from Bondage).
Hymn of Praise:
destroyer of demons, Mother of the World. The three
gods bow their heads to her, whom
<s>Śrī Rambhā</s> worships. She is the boon-granter,
giver of the three worlds; grant <s>siddhi</s> (spiritual attainment)
and fulfill my desires. The primordial maiden, riding a lion,
whom <s>Śrī Rāma</s> worships.
Chaupāī: O <s>Bandī Māī</s>, I remember you.
Remembering you, grant me knowledge and wisdom. The name
that is yours, O <s>Bandī Māī</s>, surely
you help your devotees. The three worlds

children.text: को सिरजा जबहीं । नाम धरा तिन
children.translated_text: when she created, she was given the name
<s>Bandī</s> at that very time. Gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>,

children.text: मुनि देवा । सकल करहिं बन्दी की
children.translated_text: sages, and deities — all perform the worship of <s>Bandī</s>.
The glory of <s>Bandī</s> is unfathomable and

children.text: पारा । गाढ़ परे तुम करहु उबारा ॥
children.translated_text: limitless. When in deep trouble, you deliver us.

children.text: जो बन्दी कर धरि हैं ध्याना । ता
children.translated_text: One who meditates on <s>Bandī</s>,
their welfare is eternal. Dohā:

children.text: न्दीमाई जाहिधर, ता घर भये अ
children.translated_text: <s>Bandī Māī</s>, in whichever home she resides, that home is filled with
bliss. All sorrows and conflicts are erased, and
the noose of <s>Yama</s> (death) is cut. Chaupāī: Whichever

children.text: प्रानी पर गाढ़ जु परई । बन्दीकथा
children.translated_text: being falls into great distress, let them recite the story of <s>Bandī</s>.

children.text: पाठ सो करई ॥ तुरतै होवै गाढ़उ
children.translated_text: Immediately the great difficulty
is resolved. <s>Mahādeva</s> spoke this wisdom.
<s>Bandī Māī</s>, destroyer of enemies, brilliantly
shining light, star of the world. In the three worlds
there is no other like her. Reflect and see in
your own mind. She has created all of
the world. She alone has destroyed many demons.
She alone is the mother of the three worlds.

children.text: याही दूध पूत की दाता ॥ घर २
children.translated_text: She alone is the giver of milk and sons. In every home
<s>Bandī</s> accepts worship. By taking her name, wealth and
<s>Lakṣmī</s> she bestows. She can make one poor,
she can make one wealthy. She can make one harsh, she can make one
virtuous. She alone is the giver of knowledge.
She alone is the protector of the three worlds. From her alone
comes the light of the world. With a thousand arts,
her radiance spreads. How many virtuous people
sing of you? How many destitute come to receive your charity?
<s>Śiva's</s> half-bodied consort, Mother <s>Bhavānī</s>,
a treasure of countless arts, virtues, and character.
Whoever reads this story with devotion,
<s>Bandī</s> will surely be their helper. A barren woman who hears
this story with devotion will obtain the fruit of five sons,
O brother. There was a king named <s>Kaulāpati</s>.
By no means did he obtain a son. Many
times the king meditated. Through mental effort
and prayers, he did not obtain a son. Then <s>Śaṅkara</s>
said to the king: '<s>Bandī Devī</s> resides in <s>Kāśī</s>.
Go there and meditate
on her. Be pleased and you shall obtain the fruit of a son.'
Hearing this, the king set forth to where
the pavilion of <s>Bandī</s> stood. Both husband and wife
established worship there. Then Mother
<s>Bhavānī</s> was pleased. 'Ask, ask whatever you desire,
O king. I will fulfill your purpose in every way.'
Both persons together offered a hymn of praise.
'The kingdom and all has been given to me
by you. I am most miserable, O <s>Śrī Bhava-</s>
<s>bhāminī</s> (Bhavānī). I know you are the knower of innermost hearts.'
Both persons then made a humble request:
'Grant me a son, O primordial <s>Bhavānī</s>.' A
sonless woman is greatly sorrowful. 'Show mercy
so that we may be happy.' Dohā: Then <s>Bandī</s>
was delighted and granted the king the boon of a son.
With greatly joyful hearts, the couple
then went home. Chaupāī: After some
days had passed, one son
was born to the king. In many ways
auspicious rites were performed. <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> recited the <s>Vedas</s>,
bards sang praises. Many virtuous people danced and sang;
many destitute came to receive charity.
Dohā: Diamonds, rubies, gems,
sapphires, pearls, and rubies — the king
sat and distributed them lavishly, providing for the destitute.
Chaupāī: When the son reached twelve years of age,
the king thought in his mind thus:
'Let us go and behold the feet of <s>Bhavānī</s>.
Today I shall worship her to my heart's content.' Then
the king said to the queen, 'Such joy
has arisen in my heart.' The queen said, 'This is an excellent
idea.' 'Let us go to the pavilion of <s>Bandī</s>,
O lord.' 'These good words please my heart.
By whose grace we obtained the fruit of a son.' Dohā:
When the son reached the age of twelve years, the king made
a decision: 'Now, together with all three of us,
let us go to the court of <s>Bandī</s>.' Chaupāī: With the son,
the couple proceeded to where
the pavilion of <s>Bandī</s> stood. To <s>Kāśī</s> they swiftly
came, the king. They had <s>darśana</s> (sacred viewing) together with
the assembly. A feast for a hundred thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>
was given. In many ways the king performed auspicious
rites. Dohā: Such is the <s>Bandī</s> deity,
whose glory is unfathomable and limitless. The giver of milk and sons,
she delivers from great distress. Chaupāī:
Remember her name, O brother, by whose
remembrance all doubts and worldly existence vanish. Whatever
being falls into great distress, let them hear the story of <s>Bandī</s>.
12. <s>Bandīmocāna</s>
Let them do so. Surely the great difficulty will be resolved.
<s>Śrī Śaṅkara</s> spoke thus from his holy mouth.
I tell you with love, listen all brothers. Listen to the story of <s>Bandī</s>
with devotion. <s>Bandī Devī</s>, the primordial
<s>Bhavānī</s>, giver of all <s>siddhis</s> (spiritual attainments), repository of the <s>Vedas</s>.
The sixty-four <s>yoginīs</s> sing auspicious songs;
ghosts and <s>Baitālas</s> play the <s>mṛdaṅga</s> (drum).
In this age of <s>Kali</s>, <s>Bandī Māī</s>
will surely be a helper to her devotees.
Whoever reads this tale every day, in their
home <s>Lakṣmī</s> will come and descend. Horses,
many will be tied at the gate. One will become
ruler of the three worlds. They will be
(bestower of) accomplishment of all desires. In the three worlds, whose name
[is renowned]. I bow at the feet of <s>Bandī</s>
Mother. Be a helper to the poor and destitute.
You alone are the destroyer of all enemies. In the three
worlds, [you are] the remover of sorrow. Without you,
nothing can be known. By mind, action,
and speech — I understand and say the same. Dohā: In the <s>Kali</s>
<s>Yuga</s>, <s>Bandī</s> manifests; in every home she receives
worship. Milk, sons, and <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) — whatever
one asks, she grants. Caupāī: In the city of <s>Pātāla</s> (the netherworld),
an incident occurred. <s>Ahirāvaṇa</s>
abducted <s>Rāghava</s> (Lord <s>Rāma</s>). The Lord was swiftly
taken to <s>Pātāla</s>. With great elaboration,
a sacrificial hall was prepared. For offering the sacrifice,
a plan was devised. Then the Lord remembered
<s>Bandī</s> Mother. <s>Bandī</s> then assumed a deceptive form and
appeared. At that time, <s>Hanumān</s> set forth and
went [there]. Dohā: Bringing again and again the sacrificial birds,

children.text: शठ, धरे देवि अस्थान । पूजा कि
children.translated_text: the wicked one placed them at the goddess's altar. Worship was
performed with focused mind, meditating with deep
concentration. Caupāī: Then <s>Mahirāvaṇa</s> asked
that same [question]: 'At this moment, who is
there [outside]?' Then <s>Bandī</s> was invoked.
Roaring, she came and granted the Lord her <s>darśana</s> (divine vision).
Dohā: <s>Bandī</s> Mother, upon [his] head, in dire
distress, became a helper. By her strength, <s>Hanumān</s> then
devised this plan. Caupāī: Immediately,
the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>) lifted the Lord. Then <s>Bandī</s>
gave her command. A great havoc was
wrought by <s>Hanumān</s>. <s>Mahirāvaṇa</s> was
slain as an offering. Dohā: Then they brought [everyone]
to <s>Rāma</s>, and the gods offered praise. 'Victory!
Victory throughout the three worlds!' — they abundantly showered
flowers. Then the Lord, reflecting in his heart, [said]: 'Blessed
are you, <s>Bandī</s> Mother. In such dire circumstances,
you became my helper. You alone are the savior
of the world, you are the primordial <s>Bhavānī</s>. You
are the primordial Supreme Goddess, you are the mine of virtue and
good qualities.' Thus ends the <s>Bandīmocana</s>.
The primordial <s>Bhavānī</s>, benefactress of the gods,
